title: Drugs that make the uterus contract or relax
ariaLabel: Schematic of uterine muscle contraction: oxytocin receptors, prostaglandin receptors, alpha and serotonin receptors and calcium entry all add to contraction. Oxytocin, prostaglandin analogues and ergometrine strengthen contraction, atosiban blocks oxytocin receptors, indomethacin lowers prostaglandins, and nifedipine blocks calcium entry.
caption: Schematic, not to scale. Flow and levels are qualitative and illustrative; no dose, concentration or lipid value is shown or implied.
blockInfo: A drug of the chosen class acting at this step (generic teaching symbol, not a named drug's shape). Less passes here, with the effects shown at the cholesterol and the LDL receptors.

edges.label: oxytocin receptors
edges.info: Oxytocin acts on its receptor to raise calcium in uterine muscle. Atosiban blocks this receptor to stop contractions.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: prostaglandin receptors
edges.info: Prostaglandin analogues (misoprostol, carboprost, dinoprostone) strengthen contraction and soften the cervix. NSAIDs such as indomethacin lower prostaglandin synthesis and can slow preterm labour.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: alpha and 5-HT receptors
edges.info: Ergometrine acts on alpha-adrenergic, serotonin and dopamine receptors and causes a sustained contraction used to control bleeding after delivery.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

edges.label: calcium channels
edges.info: Nifedipine blocks L-type calcium channels, so uterine muscle contracts less. This is used as a tocolytic.
Adds to the effect shown at the right.

sources: Where each class acts. Oxytocin acts at oxytocin receptors, prostaglandin analogues act at prostaglandin receptors, ergometrine acts on alpha and serotonin receptors, atosiban blocks oxytocin receptors, nifedipine blocks calcium entry and indomethacin lowers prostaglandins. This is standard teaching in the pharmacology texts the PrepNucleus lessons cite (Katzung; KD Tripathi) and were not checked against a linked source here, so they are flagged for review.
simplified: Magnesium sulphate, beta-2 agonist tocolytics, tranexamic acid, mifepristone, the third stage of labour and postpartum haemorrhage protocols, contraindications (for example ergometrine in hypertension), timing, adverse effects and monitoring are left out. Contraction is drawn as a teaching score. Levels and the size of each effect are illustrative. The drug choices are teaching toggles of a class: no named drug, dose or schedule is shown or implied, and the figure does not say who should or should not take any of them.
